agent_scope.sentence: Renin–angiotensin system (RAS) inhibitors, including angiotensin‐converting enzyme inhibitors/angiotensin receptor blockers, have been shown to reduce the risk of mortality in patients with HFrEF. 2 , 3 In addition, sacubitril‐valsartan, the first‐in‐class angiotensin receptor neprilysin (ARN) inhibitor, improves the ratio of all‐cause mortality in chronic HFrEF patients when compared with the intervention of RAS inhibitors. 4 Sodium‐glucose cotransporter‐2 (SGLT2) inhibitors, originally identified as glucose‐lowering drugs, offer important cardiorenal protections in HFrEF regardless of the diabetic status. 5 , 6 On the contrary, classic RAS inhibitors treatment could not convincingly reduce mortality in HFpEF. 7 , 8 , 9 Compared with RAS inhibitors, ARN inhibitors did not show beneficial effects in reducing total hospitalization for HF (HHF) and cardiovascular (CV) death in the status of HFpEF. 10 Recently, the improvement of mortality by SGLT2 inhibitors during the treatment of HFpEF has been identified when compared with placebo. 11 However, data directly comparing these drugs are lacking, which limits the choice of clinicians between them.
